title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Compiling a project with a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (for example a field of type Ref.Pair<int, string>) does not throw IndexOutOfRangeException or any other exception in the source generator.

The build produces no generator-crash warning (CS8785 or similar) for these member types.

expectedBehaviours: Running the MessagePack analyzers on a [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly does not throw.
No analyzer-crash diagnostic (AD0001) is reported for these member types.
The analyzer reports only the MsgPack diagnostics it would report for an equivalent same-project type, or none.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a referenced-assembly closed generic struct member finds no AD0001 and no unexpected MsgPack diagnostics.
An analyzer test covers the record struct variant in the same way.

expectedBehaviours: When a member is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly, the compiling assembly still gets its generated resolver and the formatter for the [MessagePackObject] type.
The generated output matches what is produced when the generic struct is declared in the same project, apart from type location details such as namespaces.
Serializing and deserializing an instance through the generated resolver round-trips the member value.

expectedBehaviours: A generator or analyzer exception does not end as only a build warning while the assembly silently ships without a generated resolver.
For the reported scenario the build has no crash warning and the resolver exists, so the earlier silent failure is gone.

story.what: TypeCollector stops indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] when it builds the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic for properties and the MemberNeedsKey diagnostic for fields. Both now get a null location when the member has no source declaration. The analyzer's report callback is wrapped so that a diagnostic is only passed on when its location is a source location inside the compilation being analyzed. The same hunk area also flips the condition that sets nonPublicMembersAreSerialized for attributed properties. New tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image and check that analysis and generation of a consumer project produce no diagnostics and do produce the resolver. README and MsgPack004 docs gain short notes.
story.why: Requirement MP-2283: a [MessagePackObject] member whose type is a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly made the generator and analyzer throw IndexOutOfRangeException. Metadata members have no syntax references, so indexing [0] failed. The generator crash ended up as only a warning (CS8785) and the assembly had no generated resolver.

touches.note: reportDiagnostic now wraps the analyzer callback in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation.
Diagnostic locations no longer index [0]. The condition that sets nonPublicMembersAreSerialized for attributed properties changes from != to ==.
New helper. Returns the property identifier location, or null when the property has no source declaration.
New filter. Reports a diagnostic only if its location is in source and in a syntax tree of this compilation.
New test helper. Uses a metadata-only reference, runs the verifier, then runs the generator driver directly and checks diagnostics and the resolver hint name.
New tests for the issue 2283 scenarios.

findings.title: Keyed-property accessibility check inverted, flags public members as non-public
findings.detail: In h4 the update to nonPublicMembersAreSerialized for keyed properties changed from '!= Accessibility.Public' to '== Accessibility.Public'. The requirement does not ask for this, and it contradicts the comment directly above it. The field path at line 1120 still uses '!='. As written, any [MessagePackObject] type with a public [Key] property sets the flag. That triggers MessagePackObjectAllowPrivateRequired on the attribute (line 1352). It also reports every deferred diagnostic for non-public members, and can run the partial-type check and drop the formatter (line 1382). A non-public keyed property no longer sets the flag, so its private siblings are no longer checked. Ordinary user types, which N2 says must not change, would get spurious errors, and some would lose their generated formatters.

citations.quote: if (allowPrivateAttribute is not true && (nonPublicMembersAreSerialized || ctor is { DeclaredAccessibility: not Accessibility.Public } || formattedType.GetEffectiveAccessibility() is not Accessibility.Public))

findings.title: Location filter silently drops diagnostics for source members
findings.detail: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a tree of the current compilation, including diagnostics with no location. That is broader than metadata members. GetPropertyIdentifierLocation casts with 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax', so for a positional record property declared in source (where the syntax is a ParameterSyntax) it returns null. BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is then filtered away without any notice. The MemberNeedsKey path at line 926 handles ParameterSyntax. Other in-source diagnostics that can carry a null location are also lost, such as PartialTypeRequired when the declaration is not a BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax and CollidingMemberNamesInForceMapMode. This changes existing behaviour for source types (N2) and hides problems instead of reporting them (N1).

citations.quote: var identifier = (syntax as PropertyDeclarationSyntax)?.Identifier ?? (syntax as ParameterSyntax)?.Identifier;

findings.title: No check of generated formatter output or round-trip for F3
findings.detail: The new tests turn on SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and only check that the resolver hint name exists. No snapshot compares the generated resolver and formatter with the output for the same-project case, and no runtime test round-trips an object holding a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. F3 needs the resolver to be correct, not only present. Wrong generated content from the CollectGeneric path for metadata generics would go unnoticed.

findings.title: No test with a referenced generic struct used as a field
findings.detail: The expectation covers the referenced generic type used as a property or as a field. All three new tests declare the consuming member as a property. No test uses a field of type MyGenericStruct<int> or Item<int>, so the field member path in GetObjectInfo is not exercised for this scenario.

findings.title: Generator exceptions still surface only as build warnings
findings.detail: N1 expects that a generator or analyzer failure does not end as a mere warning while the assembly ships without a resolver. The change fixes the specific IndexOutOfRangeException paths. It does nothing to catch other exceptions in TypeCollector.Collect and turn them into a clear error diagnostic. Any other unexpected exception would still appear only as CS8785 or AD0001, and the resolver would be silently missing.

refusals.reason: The README and the MsgPack004 help page now document a new contract: diagnostics about members of types from referenced assemblies are not reported in the consuming project. Whether to adopt that is for the API owners to decide.
